name: Graham polar-angle convex hull
definition: Select pivot o with minimum (y,x); sort remaining distinct points by increasing polar direction about o, then increasing squared distance. For each c, while stack has at least two points a,b and turn(a,b,c)=(b_x−a_x)(c_y−a_y)−(b_y−a_y)(c_x−a_x)≤0, pop b; append c. Return stack in counterclockwise order; return empty or singleton directly
variables: o extreme pivot; a,b stack tail; c candidate; turn signed orientation determinant
assumptions: Finite planar points, deduplicated, exact orientation and total polar order; pivot selection ensures directions lie in a half-plane
limitations: O(n log n) sorting and O(n) scan/storage; excludes intermediate collinear boundary points; collinear sets yield extreme endpoints
failure_conditions: Nonfinite coordinate, uncertain orientation or overflow
computation: Use determinant-based angle comparator and squared-distance tie order rather than rounded angles; retain only farthest point on a shared pivot ray

name: Polygon winding-number point classification
definition: For cyclic ordered vertices a,b and query q, let D=cross(b−a,q−a). Return boundary first if D=0 and q lies in the closed edge bounding box. Otherwise w=Σ_i [1(a_y≤q_y<b_y and D>0)−1(b_y≤q_y<a_y and D<0)]; classify by w≠0 for the nonzero winding rule
variables: a,b directed edge endpoints; q query; D signed orientation; w integer winding number; 1 indicator
assumptions: Finite planar closed walk with at least three vertices and exact predicates; edges implicit from successive vertices and last to first; repeated vertices allowed
limitations: O(n) time and O(1) extra space per query; winding is undefined on boundary; self-intersections use nonzero fill rule, not even-odd rule; no geographic/spherical interpretation
failure_conditions: Malformed vertices, nonfinite coordinates or unresolved boundary/orientation predicate
computation: Count upward right-ray crossings positively and downward crossings negatively; half-open vertical interval counts shared vertices once; horizontal edges contribute zero except boundary detection

source.citation: David G. Alciatore and Rick Miranda, Colorado State University, A Winding Number and Point-in-Polygon Algorithm, axis-crossing method and page 3 image reviewed; half-open convention expressed with equivalent signed predicates; https://www.engr.colostate.edu/~dga/documents/papers/point_in_polygon.pdf

name: Polygon shoelace signed area
definition: For n≥3 cyclic ordered vertices p_i=(x_i,y_i), with p_(n+1)=p_1, signed area A=½Σ_(i=1)^n(x_i y_(i+1)−x_(i+1)y_i). For a simple polygon ordinary area=|A|
variables: n vertex count; x_i,y_i Cartesian coordinates; A oriented algebraic area
assumptions: Finite planar coordinates and cyclic boundary order; simple polygon required for ordinary enclosed area; use exact or suitably controlled accumulation
limitations: O(n) time and O(1) extra space; self-crossing walks give algebraic rather than union area; cancellation and overflow may affect floating-point calculations; zero alone does not certify degeneracy or simplicity
failure_conditions: Fewer than three vertices, nonfinite coordinates, unresolved arithmetic or claiming ordinary area without simplicity
computation: Sum directed edge determinants including closing edge; optionally translate origin to improve numerical behavior; reverse orientation negates signed area

name: Ramer–Douglas–Peucker polyline simplification
definition: For ordered planar vertices p_i,…,p_j with j≥i+2, d_max=max_{i<k<j} min_{0≤t≤1} ||p_k−((1−t)p_i+t p_j)||₂. Split at first maximizing k if d_max>ε; otherwise replace subchain by endpoint chord (ε≥0). Return empty or singleton unchanged, adjacent endpoints directly
variables: p_i,p_j chord endpoints; p_k interior vertex; t segment parameter; ε nonnegative distance tolerance; d_max maximal finite-segment deviation
assumptions: Finite ordered planar vertices, finite nonnegative tolerance; exact or controlled point-to-segment comparisons; zero-length chord distance is point distance
limitations: O(n²) worst-case time, O(n log n) balanced splits, O(n) stack/output; does not guarantee topology, minimal retained vertices or a Fréchet bound; output may self-intersect
failure_conditions: Negative/nonfinite tolerance, malformed coordinate, unresolved threshold or resource exhaustion
computation: Project to chord and clamp parameter to [0,1]; when endpoints coincide use squared distance to endpoint. Compare squared distances with ε², retain first maximum on ties and concatenate recursive results without duplicate shared index

source.citation: RPI CSCI 4560/6560 Spring 2026 Lecture 23, recursive split and complexity parsed; PostGIS ST_Simplify documentation on endpoint preservation and invalid output; finite-segment convention explicitly chosen; original Ramer and Douglas–Peucker papers not reviewed; https://www.cs.rpi.edu/~cutler/classes/computationalgeometry/S26/lectures/23_curves_polyline_simplification_sprouts.pdf
